title: Data Hub Users Guide
description_raw: The City of Memphis Data Hub is a repository for accessing the City’s open datasets, dashboards, and applications. It is designed to enable the general public, internal staff, the media, and partner agencies to explore, visualize, and download data relating to the City of Memphis. The goal of the Data Hub is to support data-driven decision-making, increase transparency, and make public data easy to access. This guide provides instructions for navigating the Data Hub, finding datasets, accessing dashboards, and exporting data. The Office of Performance Management (OPM) maintains the Data Hub. Data are updated according to each dataset’s publication schedule, which varies by asset.

title: MPD Public Safety Map
description_raw: Welcome to the Public Safety map, a tool where you can explore incidents that have taken place in your neighborhood. Choose from a list of boundaries, select specific incident types, and see what has occurred near your points of interest. Want to search a specific date range? Use the date filter option to further customize your experience.Want to download the raw data? You can download the full dataset via the "download data" button located below the pins or in the Data Catalog here! If you prefer to only download a subset of the data, select the date range, boundaries, and incident type you"re interested in and click the "download selected data" button in the upper right hand corner of the overview pane.An incomplete address field can prevent an incident from being mapped or result in an incident being mapped to the wrong location. In addition, please note that due to their sensitive nature, any incidents involving sexual assault are not included in this dataset.Have questions? Be sure to check out the Memphis Data Hub Guide here!Terms of Use: The information in this portal is provided strictly as a courtesy to the public. This website provides information as to initial crime reports, and does not reflect subsequent changes in the investigation, nature, or accuracy of the initial report. While all attempts are made to ensure the correctness and suitability of information presented here, neither the City of Memphis nor the Memphis Police Department guarantee the accuracy of the information contained herein. Crime data may be amended or corrected by the Memphis Police Department at any time. This data may not reflect the official crime index totals as reported to the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation. The Memphis Police Department may, at its discretion, discontinue or modify this service at any time without notice.

title: MPD Traffic Citations
description_raw: This dataset includes both moving and non-moving citations. Data is exported daily from MPD’s server by an automated script. Data is subject to change. Traffic stop data is available in a different dataset on the Data Hub. Search the data catalog for “traffic stops”. Not all traffic stops result in a traffic citation. title: Public Safety Incidents Explorer User Guide
description_raw: The Public Safety Incidents Explorer (PSIE) was created toallow the general public, internal staff, the media, and partner agencies theability to explore recent public safety incidents responded to by the MemphisPolice Department. This user's guide provides information on how to operatethe application and obtain needed data using the map in conjunction with its filtersand tools. The Office of Performance Management (OPM) maintains thePSIE, which resides on the City of Memphis Data Hub. The map includes onlyincidents from the past three years and is updated daily at 6:00 AM. The datalag by one day and are unavailable between 2:30 and 6:00 AM while the site is updated.Historical data prior to the last three years can be found in the MPD PublicSafety Incidents dataset on the Data Hub.

title: FAQs
description_raw: FAQs Frequently Asked Questions I still have questions! Who do I contact? Do you have a User Guide available? What if I want to see data not currently on the Data Hub? How often is data updated? I need a copy of my incident report from MPD. Who I do contact? I have a question about my 311 service request. Where can I find more information? Absolutely! Please visit our User Guide page here   to see the different guides available. Great question! You have two options: first, submit an inquiry via the Contact Us form here . We can't guarantee we'll be able to release the requested data due to things like privacy concerns, workload, and data availability but feedback like this helps us prioritize what to release next. Second, you can submit a Public Records Request here and our Communications team will be in touch. This will vary by dataset. Some datasets are updated daily while others may be monthly or annually. The boundary datasets are updated on an as needed basis. Each dataset will list the update cadence on both the details page and in the attached data dictionary. Please contact Memphis Police Department Central Records office. More information is available on MPD's website here. Please visit 311.memphistn.gov here for the latest update on your service request. You can also call 311 to request an update as well. Fill out the Contact Us form here and we will be in touch within 3 business days.

title: Safer Community User Guide
description_raw: The City of Memphis has created a Safer Communities Dashboard in partnership with theMemphis Police Department (MPD). The dashboard provides detailed information on what, when, and where crime, arrests, and traffic accidents occur in the City of Memphis. The dashboard shows a time frame of three years and is updated daily. With the interactive elements, users can select the time frame, location, and type of information they wish to see.

title: Shelby County Census Tracts
description_raw:
Census Tracts are determined by the U.S. Census Bureau for calculating 
		the decennial census. Census tracts are a subdivision of the County 
		level and vary in size. Ideally a census tract contains a population of 
		4,000 people and 1,600 housing units. 249 census tracts intersect or 
		fall within the Shelby County boundary.
